newsitem.title: NIGERIA: Shell says Nigeria saboteurs spill 2,000 bbls oil.
newsitem.headline: Shell says Nigeria saboteurs spill 2,000 bbls oil.

text.p: Royal Dutch/Shell Group's Nigerian unit said on Tuesday that saboteurs had hacked into its pipeline in the troubled Niger Delta and spilled 2,000 barrels of crude oil.
"They cut open a protective cage around a pipeline manifold at Isampou, in the Ekeremo local government area and opened a drain valve to release the oil," Shell said in a statement in Lagos.

"It is one of the worst cases I have ever seen," said Shell western division general manager Joshua Udofia. "We are now trying to organise a cleanup but currently communities are preventing our emergency teams getting to the site."
The company said oil production was not affected.
Shell, the biggest oil-producing company in Nigeria, is frequently the target of attack by restive communities angry that they have not benefited from the oil produced in their backyard.

The company is currently cleaning up an oil spill in the remote village of Aleibri where 1,000 youths rallied on Saturday demanding a better deal from oil companies and threatening possible violence if the multinationals do not comply.
The spill in Aleibri occurred on March 18 and Shell says it was also caused by sabotage when a hole was drilled in a pipeline.

The Shell statement said the Isampou spill was reported on August 12 and a joint investigation team of the police, the communities' representatives, the oil authorities and Shell agreed that the cause was sabotage.
Udofia said sabotage was being used as a way of getting money from oil companies.

So far this year more than 36,500 barrels of oil have been spilled from Shell's facilities in 41 separate incidents of sabotage which accounted for 81 percent of the oil spilled from its sites, the company said.
Shell pumps around half of Nigeria's crude oil production of over two million barrels per day in a joint venture with state-run Nigerian National Petroleum Corp.
